Divide items into groups as a decision

Source: R/structured.R
part_var.Rd

Some decisions put things into groups: people into teams, jobs onto machines, parcels into vans. part_var() declares such a decision, a partition: each of n items goes into exactly one of parts groups, called parts. Items are numbered from 1 to n and parts from 1 to parts. A part may stay empty.

Usage

part_var(m, name, n, parts, start = NULL)

add_part_var(m, name, n, parts, start = NULL)

Arguments

m

A model().

name

The partition's name, unique within the model.

n

How many items; at least 1.

parts

How many parts; at least 2.

start

The division the service's search starts from: start[i] is the part of item i, a whole number from 1 to parts. Left NULL, the service chooses one.

Value

The partition, for use with part_of() and size_of().

add_part_var() returns the model, invisibly.

Details

part_of() gives the part an item is in, and size_of() how many items a part holds. Both are expressions whose values the service chooses, like the value of a decision variable. A requirement on the sizes, such as teams of two and three, is an ordinary constraint: add(m, size_of(1, teams) == 2). Data that depends on an item's part, such as what a person costs in each team, is read from a lookup_table(): cost[1:5, part_of(1:5, teams)]. Whether an item is in a given part is holds(part_of(i, teams) == t).

The answer

For each partition, the result of solve() holds res$structures$<name> with two integer vectors: part_of, the part of each item, and size_of, the number of items in each part. set_start(), evaluate() and resample() take the division from a result too.

A model with a partition is solved by a search, so its status is "heuristic".

add_part_var() declares the partition in the same way but returns the model, for use in a pipe; m$name then retrieves the partition.

Examples

# Six players of strengths 7, 5, 4, 3, 2 and 1 form a team of four and a
# team of two, as evenly matched as possible.
strength <- c(7, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1)                         # of players 1 to 6
m <- model()
teams <- part_var(m, "teams", 6, 2)                     # 6 players into teams 1 and 2
in_team <- function(t) holds(part_of(1:6, teams) == t)  # 1 for each player in team t
add(m, size_of(1, teams) == 4)                          # team 1 has four players
minimize(m, max(sum(strength * in_team(1)), sum(strength * in_team(2))))
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res <- solve(m)
res$objective                                           # 11
res$structures$teams$part_of                            # 2 1 2 1 1 1: players 1 and 3 form team 2
res$structures$teams$size_of                            # 4 2
} # }
